_comment: Civil Engineering problems (real-world problems, never one student's project). IDs must be unique across all problem files.

problems.title: Safe, affordable buildings for growing towns
problems.description: Schools, hostels, offices, hospitals and homes in fast-growing towns need multi-storey buildings that are safe, economical and built to code. Poor design and ageing structures lead to defects, costly repairs and collapse risk.

problems.title: Bridges and safe crossings over rivers and roads
problems.description: Rivers, valleys and busy roads cut communities off from markets, schools and hospitals, especially in the rainy season. Durable, affordable bridges and pedestrian crossings keep people and goods moving safely.

problems.title: Costly or poor-quality building materials
problems.description: Cement, sand and aggregates are expensive and their quality varies by source, which weakens concrete, blocks and bricks. Local and waste materials can cut cost and environmental impact if their strength and durability are proven.

problems.title: Weak and expansive soils under roads and buildings
problems.description: Black cotton and other expansive or weak soils swell, shrink and lose strength when wet, cracking roads and foundations. Stabilising them cheaply, often with local or waste materials, extends the life of what is built on them.

problems.title: Roads that fail early and cost too much to maintain
problems.description: Many roads rut, crack and pothole long before their design life because of poor materials, drainage and heavy loads. Better pavement design, materials and maintenance planning lower the cost of keeping roads usable.
any: drainage system effectiveness on flexible pavement

problems.title: Traffic congestion and unsafe junctions in cities
problems.description: Growing cities face long queues at junctions, poor parking and mixed traffic that slows buses and endangers pedestrians. Better junction design, signals, parking and public transport priority keep traffic moving safely.

problems.title: Water scarcity and unreliable supply
problems.description: Villages, schools and fast-growing towns often lack a reliable water source, and supply networks lose much of what they carry. Harvesting rainwater, finding groundwater and designing efficient supply systems close the gap.

problems.title: Flooding and poor storm water drainage
problems.description: Heavy rain overwhelms blocked or undersized drains, flooding streets, homes and roads. Hydraulic modelling and well-designed drainage and flood control structures reduce damage and disease.

problems.title: Construction projects that run late and over budget
problems.description: Building and road projects often finish late, cost more than planned or are abandoned, because of late payments, poor planning, rework and skill shortages. Better project, cost and quality management protects public money.
